page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 40 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 40 dedicated vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.8 GB of memory per core, and operates on the KVM hypervisor. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results position this instance in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-intensive tasks, it achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. For database and key-value operations, the instance handles 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 14249.04 in PassMark database operations.

The absence of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators limits this instance's utility for direct high-speed local data caching or heavy parallelized deep learning tasks. However, the dedicated core allocation and 3.1 GHz clock speed offer stable compute density. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring predictable CPU performance without the overhead of hyperthreading. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, static web serving, and small to medium-scale language model inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 server instance featuring 40 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. It is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM (4.8 GB per core), 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage or GPU accelerators. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers stable, non-hyperthreaded compute performance. Benchmark data shows a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 166.28 GB/sec. It processes Redis SET operations at 34.78 million operations per second and handles small-model LLM prompt processing at 1841.39 tokens/sec. This hardware profile is suited for compute-intensive tasks, software compilation, database operations, and web serving where dedicated CPU resources are required without the need for local NVMe storage.
